history.dynasty: Hoysala Empire (attributed); the style also shows Western Chalukyan influence; the region was ruled successively by Gangas, Cholas, Chalukyas, Uchchangi Pandyas and Hoysalas
history.period: 11th century CE (attributed, weakly documented); the temple is mentioned in 12th-century Pandya and 13th-century Hoysala inscriptions; restored with mud walls and plaster in 1912
history.summary: Sri Eshwara Temple is a small Hoysala-era Shiva temple at Anekonda village, a suburb of Davangere town off the Davangere-Jagalur highway (CSV town 'Davangere' is imprecise - the temple is at Anekonda, not in Davangere city itself). Anekonda's name is said to come from elephants being tied here when Bethuru was the Chalukya capital. The temple was originally planned as a dwikuta (two-shrine) temple on a raised platform and was later converted into a trikuta; only two cells are extant now (the south cell collapsed at some point, and one mukhamandapa was converted into a garbhagriha during renovation). Its architectural highlights include a Gajalakshmi figure on the garbhagriha doorway lintel, niches with female chauri-bearers flanking the sukanasi doorway (Sarasvati on the right, Mahishasuramardini on the left), and the navaranga's central ceiling bearing an exquisitely carved Gajasurasamhara panel flanked by Vishnu and Brahma, with 12 Adityas above and 7 Shiva ganas below playing music. The outer side was restored with mud walls and plaster in 1912 (per the Karnataka archaeology department). NOTE: several travel sites (Holidify, TripHobo) list a generic 'Eshwara Temple' at Nittuvalli, Davangere with mud-plaster construction and two cells - this may be the same Anekonda temple described imprecisely, since Nittuvalli is nearby; identity conflation possible (verify).

name: Eshwara Temple
town: Anekonda (CSV town 'Davangere' is imprecise - the temple is at Anekonda village, a suburb of Davangere town off the Davangere-Jagalur highway, Davangere taluk)
town_description: Anekonda is a village suburb of Davangere city on the Davangere-Jagalur highway in central Karnataka, about 5 km from the city centre. It is historically notable as the place where elephants were tied when Bethuru was the Chalukya capital, and its chief attraction is the 11th-century Hoysala Sri Eshwara Temple, documented by the Karnataka archaeology department.

travel.road: Off the Davangere-Jagalur highway at Anekonda, a suburb of Davangere; reachable by taxi/auto from Davangere city (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (winter/pleasant season) is the best time to visit central Karnataka; the temple is a heritage monument visitable year-round.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed on place databases as roughly 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily (verify - not confirmed by an official temple source). Entry appears to be informal with local priests conducting pooja programs.
